evidence.quote: Edible podded peas (mange tout): Oregon Sugar Pod II is sometimes grown for its edible pods, and is harvested when the pods are fully sized, but before the young seeds start swelling (snow peas).

varieties.name: Sugar Daddy

evidence.quote: Sugar Daddy is also grown for its edible pod, but is harvested when the seeds have swollen (sugar peas).

highveld.text: Cold areas with late frosts: plant in July, so flowering starts after frost risk passes — flowers and young pods are frost-sensitive even though mature plants tolerate cold.

evidence.quote: In cold areas which experience late frosts, planting in July is usually best.

high-mountain.text: Treated as the same 'cold areas, late frosts' case as highveld (July planting) — not separately confirmed for this zone.

midlands-mistbelt.text: Falls under the source's general 'most other areas' guidance: plant May-June.

evidence.quote: In most other areas, planting is done from May to June.

western-cape.text: Matches the source's 'few selected areas with cool autumns, winters and early summers, light or no frost' — planting can stretch March-July. This is this pass's zone assignment (winter-rainfall Mediterranean fits that climate description); the source itself names no province.

evidence.quote: In a few selected areas, with cool autumns, winters and early summers, and which experience only light or no frosts, planting may stretch from March to July.

southern-cape.text: Same inferred fit as western-cape (mild, light/no-frost climate) — not independently confirmed for this zone by name.

gaps: No cultivar is tied to a named zone anywhere in the source — cultivars are grouped only by end-use (processing / fresh / edible-podded), so all 'zones' arrays above are empty rather than guessed.

No sourced recommendation at all for lowveld-bushveld, subtropical-coast or karoo-arid — peas are described as a cool-season crop throughout and the source does not address hot/frost-free or arid production.
Length-of-crop (70-120 days depending on temperature) and yield (1.5-10 t/ha depending on market/type) are sourced but not broken out by zone or cultivar.
